about: Provenance of the committed v3 corpus artifacts: pinned upstream sources, a HERMETIC toolchain (the container base pinned by OCI manifest digest, the exact package NEVRAs, and a pinned JDK — see Containerfile), the compat patches, and the SHA-256 of every produced artifact. Rebuilding with build/build-all.sh from these exact inputs reproduces the committed bytes: verified byte-for-byte on 2026-08-22 for all 11 artifacts. The recipe's only non-hermetic input is the FEDORA PACKAGE REPOSITORY itself (live metadata): the NEVRA pins make the toolchain deterministic while the repository continues to serve those exact packages, so a rebuild needs network for dnf exactly as it needs network for the source fetch. A repository-snapshot-pinned build or a published OCI image by digest would remove even that dependency; the committed artifact hashes remain the corpus's ground truth either way.

compat_patches.patch: CFLAGS=-std=gnu89 (era-correct C semantics; gcc 14+ defaults to C23 where f() means f(void))

compat_patches.impact: terminal-UI code only, never linked into the probe
compat_patches.patch: sed 's/-DTERMIO //' Configure; sed 's/# define TERMIO/# define TERMIOS/' crypto/ui/ui_openssl.c (termio.h removed from modern glibc)

note: The heartbleed probe (heartbleed/src/hb.c) is linked against each library set with -no-pie (the container archives are built without -fPIC).

toolchain.java: openjdk 17.0.17 (2025-10-21) — the PINNED in-image JDK the probe is compiled with; no host javac is involved
toolchain.reproducibility: verified 2026-08-22: a rebuild from these exact inputs (pinned base digest + pinned NEVRAs + pinned sources) reproduced all 11 committed artifact hashes byte-for-byte; the probe.jar was rebuilt in-image with the pinned JDK (its behavior is unchanged: JNDI_LOOKUP_ATTEMPTED on 2.14.1, JNDI_LOOKUP_NOT_ATTEMPTED on 2.17.1)
